title: VPN & Proxy Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to maximize your VPN and proxy privacy protection. Harden your setup, avoid common mistakes, and stay truly anonymous online.
intro: Using a VPN or proxy isn't enough for true privacy. This comprehensive checklist helps you properly configure and harden your setup to prevent leaks, maximize anonymity, and avoid common security pitfalls that could expose your identity.

items.task: Choose a verified no-log VPN provider
items.why: Many VPNs claim no-logs but haven't been independently audited. Real no-log providers protect you if servers are compromised.
items.howTo: Research providers with public audits (ExpressVPN, NordVPN, Surfshark). Avoid free VPNs that sell data. Check for third-party security audits and transparency reports.

items.why: If your VPN disconnects, your real IP address gets exposed to websites and your ISP without a kill switch.
items.howTo: Go to VPN app settings and enable 'Kill Switch' or 'Network Lock'. Test by disconnecting VPN - internet should stop working until VPN reconnects.

items.why: Older protocols like PPTP and L2TP have known vulnerabilities. Modern protocols provide better encryption and security.
items.howTo: In VPN settings, select OpenVPN (most compatible) or WireGuard (faster, newer). Avoid PPTP, L2TP/IPSec, and IKEv2 when possible.

items.why: IPv6 can bypass VPN tunnels, leaking your real location and identity even when VPN is active.
items.howTo: Disable IPv6 in your router/device network settings. On Windows: Network Settings > Change adapter options > Disable IPv6. Test for leaks at ipleak.net.

items.why: Using your ISP's DNS servers can leak browsing activity and location even through a VPN tunnel.
items.howTo: Set VPN to use its own DNS or configure privacy-focused DNS like Cloudflare (1.1.1.1) or Quad9 (9.9.9.9). Verify no DNS leaks at dnsleaktest.com.

items.why: Choosing servers in countries with strong data retention laws or far distances impacts both privacy and performance.
items.howTo: Choose servers in privacy-friendly countries (Switzerland, Iceland, Netherlands). Balance distance vs privacy needs. Avoid Five Eyes countries for sensitive activities.

items.why: HTTP proxies don't encrypt traffic, making your data visible to anyone monitoring the connection.
items.howTo: Configure browser or applications to use HTTPS or SOCKS5 proxies only. Avoid HTTP and transparent proxies. Verify encryption at whatismyipaddress.com.

items.why: Many proxy services log user activity and can be compelled to share data with authorities or sell it to third parties.
items.howTo: Read privacy policies carefully. Choose providers with explicit no-log policies. Test with residential proxies from reputable providers like Bright Data or Smartproxy.

items.why: Using the same proxy creates patterns that can be tracked and linked back to your real identity over time.
items.howTo: Set up automatic proxy rotation every 10-30 minutes. Use proxy management tools or browser extensions that rotate servers from different locations automatically.

items.why: Unsecured proxies can be used by anyone, increasing the risk of being associated with malicious activities from other users.
items.howTo: Use proxies that require username/password authentication. Set up unique credentials for each proxy service. Enable IP whitelisting when available.

items.task: Test for WebRTC and DNS leaks
items.why: Proxies may not route all traffic types, allowing your real IP to leak through WebRTC or DNS requests.
items.howTo: Visit browserleaks.com and ipleak.net to test for leaks. Disable WebRTC in browser settings or use extensions like WebRTC Leak Shield.

items.task: Use a privacy-focused browser for enhanced privacy
items.why: Regular browsers leak data through fingerprinting, cookies, and tracking. Privacy-focused browsers provides built-in privacy protections.
items.howTo: Use a privacy-focused browser configure it as your primary browser for sensitive activities. Enable all privacy features and use with your VPN/proxy setup.

items.why: WebRTC can reveal your real IP address even when using VPN or proxy, completely bypassing your privacy protection.
items.howTo: In Chrome/Edge: use extension 'WebRTC Leak Shield'. Firefox: type about:config, set media.peerconnection.enabled to false. Test at browserleaks.com/webrtc.

items.task: Clear cookies and browser data regularly
items.why: Persistent cookies and stored data can be used to track you across sessions even when your IP address changes.
items.howTo: Set browser to clear all data on exit. Use incognito/private mode for sensitive browsing. Install extensions like Cookie AutoDelete for automatic cleanup.

items.why: Some applications may bypass system-wide proxy settings, potentially leaking your real IP address and location.
items.howTo: Configure proxy settings individually in each application. For torrent clients, email clients, and browsers, verify proxy settings are active and working correctly.

items.why: Browsers can request your physical location through GPS, WiFi, and cell tower data, overriding VPN/proxy location masking.
items.howTo: In browser settings, disable location sharing. Block geolocation requests by default. In system settings, disable location services for browsers and apps.

items.task: Monitor for IP and DNS leaks regularly
items.why: VPN and proxy configurations can break due to updates or network changes, exposing your real identity without warning.
items.howTo: Weekly tests at ipleak.net, dnsleaktest.com, and browserleaks.com. Set up automated monitoring tools or browser bookmarks for quick testing.

items.task: Use different VPN/proxy for different activities
items.why: Using the same service for all activities creates linkable patterns that can compromise your privacy across different use cases.
items.howTo: Use separate VPN accounts for streaming, work, and sensitive browsing. Consider using Tor for maximum anonymity alongside VPN for extremely sensitive activities.

items.task: Enable VPN obfuscation in restricted networks
items.why: Some networks block VPN traffic entirely, and governments can detect and restrict VPN usage through deep packet inspection.
items.howTo: Enable obfuscation/stealth mode in VPN settings. Use providers with specialized servers for China/Iran. Consider Shadowsocks or obfs4 protocols.

items.task: Configure firewall rules for VPN-only traffic
items.why: If VPN fails, applications might continue using your regular internet connection, exposing your activities and location.
items.howTo: Set firewall to block all traffic except through VPN interface. On Windows use VPN client firewalls. Linux users can configure iptables rules for VPN-only routing.

items.why: Apps with excessive permissions can leak location data, contacts, and personal information that compromises your privacy efforts.
items.howTo: Review app permissions monthly. Deny location, contacts, and network access to unnecessary apps. Use permission managers like App Ops for granular control.

pro_tips: Test your setup using multiple leak detection websites - different sites check for different types of leaks and vulnerabilities.
Consider chaining VPN + Tor for maximum anonymity, but expect significantly slower speeds for this double-layer protection.
Use different email addresses and payment methods when signing up for VPN services to avoid creating linkable digital footprints.
Keep a backup VPN service active - if your primary service goes down, you won't be exposed while finding alternatives.
Document your configuration settings - when troubleshooting or switching devices, you'll want to replicate your secure setup exactly.
